title: Fix SQL injection vulnerability in controller sort parameters
description:
All controller index actions use unsanitized params[:sort] directly in .order() calls, allowing arbitrary SQL injection.

Example (ProductsController:17, NichesController:14, etc.):
  products.order(params[:sort] || 'created_at DESC')

An attacker can inject SQL: ?sort=id);DROP TABLE products;--
acceptance_criteria:
- Implement whitelist of allowed sort columns per controller
- Sanitize sort direction (asc/desc only)
- Return 400 Bad Request for invalid sort parameters
- Add tests for SQL injection attempts
close_reason: Fixed: all controllers use sanitize_sort_params with column whitelist, direction validation, and comprehensive SQL injection tests

title: Add listing traction classification service object
description:
## Context & Problem
Listings need automatic traction classification based on their metrics. This business logic should be in a service object, not controllers. Used by Listing Performance Dashboard and alerts.

## Requirements
1. Create Listings::ClassifyTraction service object
2. Classification rules (from product-discovery-process.md):
   - Scaling: any organic sale within 14 days of listing
   - Promising: fav/view ratio > 5%, no sale yet
   - No signal: views > 100, fav/view < 5%, no sale
   - New: less than 7 days old with insufficient data
3. Read thresholds from Settings if available, fall back to defaults
4. Return classification with: label, icon, color, recommended_action
5. Batch classify method for efficiency (classify all active listings at once)
6. Optional: update listing with traction_status field

## Files Affected

- backend/test/services/listings/classify_traction_test.rb (new)
- backend/app/models/listing.rb (add traction_status if needed)

## Testing

- [ ] Correctly classifies promising listings (high fav/view, no sale)
- [ ] Correctly classifies no-signal listings (high views, low engagement)
- [ ] Handles new listings gracefully
- [ ] Batch classification works
- [ ] Threshold overrides from Settings work
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Service correctly classifies all 4 traction states
- [ ] Thresholds configurable via Settings
